Let
\[
L_h
\]
be the minimum length of a complete reduction of \(T_h\). The answer is
\[
\boxed{
M_h=
\prod_{k=1}^{h-1}
\binom{2^{k+1}-k-2}{2^k-1}
\prod_{k=1}^{h-1}
\binom{2^k-2}{2^{k-1}-1}^{\,2^{h-k}-1}
}
\]
with the convention that an empty product is \(1\). Thus \(M_1=1\).

To justify this, write \(T_k\) as a “prefix” placed before some tail \(R\). In a shortest reduction of
\[
b(T_k,R),
\]
each internal node of the prefix \(T_k\) must be rotated exactly once, and an internal node can be rotated only after all its ancestors in \(T_k\) have already been rotated. No shortest reduction ever benefits from reducing below such a node first.

So the prefix contributes a poset \(P_k\): the internal nodes of the complete binary tree of height \(k\), ordered by ancestor-before-descendant. Its size is
\[
a_k=2^k-1.
\]
Let \(D_k\) be the number of linear extensions of \(P_k\). Since \(P_k\) consists of a root followed by two independent copies of \(P_{k-1}\),
\[
D_0=1,\qquad
D_k=\binom{2a_{k-1}}{a_{k-1}}D_{k-1}^2
=\binom{2^k-2}{2^{k-1}-1}D_{k-1}^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
D_k=\prod_{i=1}^{k}
\binom{2^i-2}{2^{i-1}-1}^{2^{k-i}}.
\]

Now \(T_h=b(T_{h-1},T_{h-1})\). The left copy contributes \(P_{h-1}\), while the right copy must itself be reduced optimally. These two processes can be interleaved freely. Also
\[
L_1=0,\qquad
L_h=L_{h-1}+a_{h-1},
\]
so
\[
L_h=\sum_{j=1}^{h-1}(2^j-1)=2^h-h-1.
\]
Thus
\[
M_h=M_{h-1}D_{h-1}\binom{L_h}{a_{h-1}}
=
M_{h-1}D_{h-1}
\binom{2^h-h-1}{2^{h-1}-1}.
\]
Expanding this recurrence gives exactly
\[
\boxed{
M_h=
\prod_{k=1}^{h-1}
\binom{2^{k+1}-k-2}{2^k-1}
\prod_{k=1}^{h-1}
\binom{2^k-2}{2^{k-1}-1}^{\,2^{h-k}-1}
}.
\]

For example,
\[
M_1=1,\quad M_2=1,\quad M_3=8,\quad M_4=211200.
\]
